description: Batched row mutations in the Svelte 5 data grid with api.applyTransaction({ add, update, remove }), the high-frequency streaming path. One call applies inserts, updates and removals in a single data update, far cheaper than addRow or setCellValue per row; update and remove match rows by getRowId and remove also accepts row references. The demo ticks a live order book through batched transactions.
keywords: svelte grid add update remove rows

faq.question: When should I use applyTransaction instead of setting data?
faq.answer: When you have a stream of small changes. Replacing the whole array makes the grid diff every row; a transaction tells it exactly which rows were added, changed or removed, so a tick with fifty updates costs fifty row renders.

faq.question: How are updated rows matched?
faq.answer: By the id from getRowId. Pass the updated row object in update and the grid replaces the row with that id; remove takes ids or row references.

faq.question: What does the call return?
faq.answer: Counts of the rows actually added, updated and removed, which the demo accumulates into a running total; api.getData() reflects the new state immediately.
